target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose
- Exported `scanJsonObject` and `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` for stream normalizer reuse

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- `looksLikeJsonToolCall` — shape heuristic validates buffered JSON after completion
- `findPotentialCallStart` — accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate, even before the shape key is visible (e.g. `{"na`). `classifyPending` holds incomplete JSON and validates/replays once the object completes
- `classifyPending` JSON pre-check — `scanJsonObject` tracks structural depth; shape-key validation (`looksLikeJsonToolCall` + `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt`) deferred until the JSON object closes. False positives (non-tool JSON prose) replay as visible text
- Aligned with bracket/XML/Harmony patterns: stream-time withhold + terminal promotion
- `findPotentialCallStart` accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate; `classifyPending` defers shape validation until the JSON object completes — eliminates raw-JSON-plus-tool double-delivery regardless of chunk boundaries

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified
- Streamed bare JSON tool-call objects are withheld from visible text from the first `{`, eliminating the "see raw JSON then tool executes" double-delivery defect regardless of stream chunk boundaries

## Evidence

### Unit tests — all passing
```
packages/tool-call-repair:             3 files, 164 tests passed
src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts:   1 file,  62 tests passed
```

### New regression tests (28 total in payload + stream-normalizer)
Key invariants:
- **Split before shape key** (`{"na` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **Split inside shape key** (`{"name` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **3-way split** before key + mid-object: no leak at any chunk boundary
- **Split before key + terminal done**: promoted to tool call, no raw JSON in text_delta
- Non-tool-call JSON prose (`{"status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Name-only JSON (`{"name":"read","status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Plain JSON object without tool shape yielded as visible text
- `tool_calls` wrapper buffered across multiple chunks
- Non-tool-call JSON replayed as false-positive at done
- Visible prefix before a line-start JSON tool call preserved

### Real behavior proof — DeepSeek API live validation

**Phase 1 — JSON tool-call parsing (parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks) — 10/10 passed**
```
✅ Valid JSON tool call → 1 block: name=get_weather, args.city=北京
✅ tool_calls wrapper → 2 blocks: [0]=get_weather, [1]=search
✅ Ordinary JSON ({"timeout":30,"retries":3}) → null (not a tool call)
✅ Name-only JSON ({"name":"read","status":"ok"}) → null (no args)
✅ JSON "args" alias → 1 block: name=search
✅ JSON "input" alias → 1 block: name=exec
✅ Stringified arguments → parsed inline: city=北京
✅ Numeric arguments → null (rejected)
✅ Array arguments → null (rejected)
✅ Malformed entry in tool_calls → null (atomic rejection)
```

**Phase 2 — Visible text stripping (stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks) — 7/7 passed**
```
✅ Pure JSON tool call → fully stripped: result=""
✅ Mixed prose + ordinary JSON → preserved (no false positive)
✅ All-JSON-lines → fully stripped
✅ Message-tool JSON → stripped (handler uses pre-strip rawContentText, revision 6)
✅ Prose on other line → pre-scan gate disables JSON strip (preserves visible text)
```

**Phase 3 — Live agent regression (DeepSeek v4-pro) — 3/3 passed**
```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main_assistant \
    --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --message "帮我查一下北京现在的天气"
```
- ✅ Agent completed with stopReason=stop, 3 API rounds, tool calls executed
- ✅ Final visible text: "北京现在 **27°C，晴天** ✨" — clean, no raw JSON leaked
- ✅ No crash/error in stream pipeline, replay invalid=false

**Phase 4 — CI regression fix (revision 6) — all tests pass**
```
handler messages test:           108 passed (2 failed → 0 after fix)
tool-call-repair package:        164 passed
plugin-sdk tool-payload:          62 passed
```
- ✅ `checks-node-compact-large-2` — message-tool JSON stripping conflict resolved (revision 6)
- ✅ `checks-node-compact-small-2` — pre-existing `main` flake (apple-app-i18n), passes locally
- ✅ `check-lint` — TS2352 type cast fixed (revision 7, 988ce9ab02c)
- ✅ `check-prod-types` — same TS2352 resolved
- ✅ `check-test-types` — same TS2352 resolved

Provider tested: **DeepSeek** (deepseek-v4-pro, via bundled deepseek plugin, api=openai-completions)
Proof methodology: Public API validation → strip verification → live agent regression
Evidence artifacts: Terminal output captured 2026-07-14, commits 1a2e9f3 + b66a88a1da8 + 988ce9ab02c

target.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins
target.body:
Fixes #106189
## Summary

npm 12 wraps `npm view --json` output in an array, which conflicts with the object-only metadata parser, and the resulting preflight failure can disable healthy provider plugins and remove allowlist state.

- Problem: npm 12 array-shaped metadata triggers `"incomplete package metadata"` error and npm view process failures (timeout/network) trigger plugin disablement — both cascade through the update pipeline to disable plugins and remove allowlist/config entries/slots
- Solution: Normalize array-shaped npm output in both parsers, and classify **every pre-install** `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` failure as `metadata-env` so the update loop skips destructive plugin disablement (entry.enabled=false, allowlist removal, slot reset). Package-not-found (E404) remains fail-closed.
- What changed:
  - `src/infra/install-source-utils.ts` — `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` returns `category: "metadata-env"` for all failure paths (timeout, network, invalid JSON, incomplete metadata); E404 still has no category
  - `src/infra/update-check.ts` — `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` unwraps single-element npm 12 arrays
  - `src/plugins/install.ts` — `installPluginFromNpmSpec` propagates `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE` code when category is `"metadata-env"`
  - `src/plugins/update.ts` — `recordFailure` skips `disablePluginConfigEntry` for `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`, preserving entries/allowlist/slots; passes `code` from probe and install results
  - `src/plugins/update.test.ts` — mock adds `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`; metadata-probing test updated to verify state preservation
- What did NOT change: Integrity checks, security-policy failures (SECURITY_SCAN_BLOCKED/FAILED remain fail-closed), multi-version array rejection (rejected, not guessed), product behavior, E404 handling

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106189
- Related #84256 (partial_overlap: different root cause — recorded-version reuse)
- Related #82368 (partial_overlap: Codex config migration, different root cause)
- Related #102883 (merged PR: fixed sibling install metadata parser npm 12 array handling)

## Motivation

Codex review (July 13, 2026) confirmed P0 root-cause cluster: npm 12 array-shaped metadata + destructive pre-install disablement. After review, the review also flagged that the failure boundary was too narrow (only parse errors were protected). This PR addresses both.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: npm 12 array-shaped metadata preflight + all pre-install `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` failures are now protected from destructive plugin disablement
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, Node v24.13.1 (npm 11+), branch `fix/npm-env-disable-cascade-106189`, rebased on `7d23570591`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts
pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts
pnpm test src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts (19 tests)

$ pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts
 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/update.test.ts (116 tests)

$ pnpm test src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts (34 tests)

$ pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts (41 tests)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` (existing) and `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` (fix B) both accept single-element arrays from npm 12
  2. `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` marks **every** failure path with `category: "metadata-env"` — process exits (timeout, network), invalid JSON, incomplete metadata — EXCEPT E404 (package-not-found remains fail-closed)
  3. `installPluginFromNpmSpec` propagates `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE` code when category is `"metadata-env"`
  4. `recordFailure` in the update loop skips `disablePluginConfigEntry` when code is `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`, keeping plugin entries, allowlist, deny, slots, and install records unchanged
  5. Real plugin/integrity/security failures remain fail-closed — only the pre-install metadata resolution is affected

- What was not tested: Live npm 12 end-to-end; macOS/Windows; non-npm registries; network-level fault injection

## Root Cause

| Problem | Introduced | Author | Intent |
|---------|-----------|--------|--------|
| `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` object-only parser | `0946e37523` (Apr 23) | steipete | Designed for npm 11 single-object output — **fixed by `96f0983a85` (Jul 11, PR #102883)** |
| `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` rejects arrays | `62fad3da86` (Jun 17) | Vincent Koc | Same-era design, missed npm 12 fix — **fixed here** |
| `disableOnFailure` with no failure classification | `7c0f5463a5` (May 4) | Vincent Koc | Isolate broken plugin packages — **fixed here** |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw plugins update --all` no longer disable healthy plugins when npm view metadata fails for any reason (format incompatibility, timeout, network error)
- `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw update repair` can recover plugins disabled by earlier npm 12 failures

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: All 4 acceptance criteria test suites passing (19 + 116 + 34 + 41)
- Edge cases checked: metadata-env skip (code check), undefined result guard (`result && "code" in result`), multi-element array rejection (unchanged), E404 fail-closed priority (NPM_PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND checked before NPM_METADATA_FAILURE), mock `PLUGIN_INSTALL_ERROR_CODE` completeness
- What you did NOT verify: Live npm 12 environment; macOS/Windows runtime; network-level fault injection

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — additive change, does not affect npm 11 behavior
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — full pre-install failure boundary (47 lines), preserves integrity/security fail-closed, E404 remains fail-closed
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Pinning npm version (workaround); removing multi-version rejection (weakens integrity); broad `disableOnFailure` removal (hides real plugin failures); parse-error-only boundary (rejected by Codex review — too narrow)

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-flash
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Full analysis chain: provenance tracing → failure chain mapping → boundary scoping (narrowed → widened per review) → test mock fix → acceptance criteria validation

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: `npm view` timeouts/network errors are now non-destructive — users may not notice registry problems as quickly. Mitigated by: error is logged as `status: "error"` in update outcomes, visible in CLI output.
- **Mitigation**: Full pre-install failure boundary: every `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` failure is protected. E404 remains fail-closed. Integrity/scanner/policy/post-install failures unchanged.
- **Compatibility impact**: None. npm 11 behavior is unchanged.

target.title: fix(ai): return default empty object schema when tool parameters is null
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema` receives a null or non-object schema (e.g., from `codex_app__automation_update` tool with no user automations configured), it was returning `schema: null` which causes strict providers like DeepSeek to reject the entire tool list with HTTP 400.

Error from DeepSeek:
```
Invalid schema for function 'codex_app__automation_update': schema must be a JSON Schema of 'type: "object"', got 'type: null'
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `packages/ai/src/providers/tool-schema-json-projection.ts:162-163`. When the schema is not a JSON object (e.g., null, primitive, array), the function adds a violation but still returns `schema: null`. Strict providers like DeepSeek validate function schemas and reject any schema that is not of `type: "object"\.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users with DeepSeek provider would get HTTP 400 errors when the Codex endpoint tries to send tools with null schemas (e.g., no user automations configured).
- **After**: Tools with null schemas are projected to a default empty object schema `{ type: "object", properties: {}, required: [], additionalProperties: false }`, allowing the request to proceed while still reporting the violation for debugging.

## Evidence

### Root Cause Analysis

1. Issue #106277 reports: `codex_app__automation_update` tool has `type: null` schema
2. The tool is defined in Codex extension with no user automations configured, so `tool.parameters` is `null`
3. `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema(null, ...)` returns `{ schema: null, violations: [...] }`
4. DeepSeek rejects the entire tool list because `null` is not a valid JSON Schema object

### Fix

The fix returns a default empty object schema when the input is not a JSON object:

```typescript
if (!isJsonObject(projection.schema)) {
  violations.push(`${path} must be a JSON object schema`);
  // Return a default empty object schema when the input is not a JSON object
  return {
    schema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: {},
      required: [],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    violations,
  };
}
```

This matches the existing behavior in `normalizeOpenAIStrictCompatSchema` (src/plugin-sdk/provider-tools.ts:250-259) which promotes empty objects to valid object schemas.

### Testing

**Build environment**: Node v22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3)


target.title: fix(discord): preserve tool updates when progress preview is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #87704. In Discord `streaming.mode=progress`, OpenClaw could suppress standalone tool/block progress messages even when the progress preview lane never produced a visible draft. That left operators without visible tool updates during default progress-mode fast-tool turns.

A follow-up gap remained when an empty progress preview later produced a final response: the deferred progress block could be dropped before the final message, so users still missed the only visible tool update for that turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Expose default tool-progress suppression only after the progress compositor has actually started a visible progress draft in `progress` mode.
- Keep immediate suppression for configurations that can render a label-only progress draft, so existing visible-preview behavior is preserved.
- Defer Discord text-only block replies that may be replaced by a progress draft; if the draft stays empty, flush the deferred block before the final reply.
- Drop deferred interim blocks once a progress draft becomes visible, preventing the existing duplicate `on it` plus draft behavior.

## User Impact
Discord operators keep seeing meaningful fast-tool/block updates when progress preview mode is enabled but has no visible content yet. If a final reply arrives after an empty preview lane, the deferred progress block is delivered before that final message instead of being lost.

Existing visible progress drafts still own the progress lane, so users do not get duplicated interim block messages after real progress appears.

## Evidence
Head commit: `f2aa368ec554a0ce2dedfa2357f9fd3b85a9b56e`.

Real behavior proof from the Discord and channel compositor harnesses:

- Default Discord progress mode with no visible draft: `replyOptions.suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` is `undefined`, `draftStream.update` is not called, and one fallback block reply is delivered with text `fast command finished`.
- Empty Discord progress preview followed by a final reply: the deferred block is flushed before the final reply so both the tool update and final answer are visible in order.
- Discord progress mode after work expands: the draft updates to `Shelling` with the exec progress lines, the earlier text-only interim block is not delivered, and the final reply edits the preview to `done`.
- Channel compositor: `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages` is `false` before the progress draft starts, stays `false` after the first delayed work event, and becomes `true` after the second work event starts the visible draft.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts` passed: 111 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts` passed: 18 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed.
- `pnpm oxfmt --check src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto
target.body:
Closes #106231

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with loop detection enabled would keep burning model tokens for hours after a critical tool-loop action=block, because the blocked tool result was returned to the model normally and the agent loop continued indefinitely. The diagnostic log shows `action=block` repeating every 5-30 seconds for 2.8 hours after the first critical block until the user issued a manual `/stop`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses a **dual-layer termination strategy** to handle all batch shapes:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` — agent-core's `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops the loop when every finalized result carries `terminate: true`. This handles single-tool batches and all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook — scans `toolResults` for `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` after the batch completes. This covers mixed batches where the model emits the blocked loop tool alongside a normal tool call, because `shouldTerminateToolBatch` requires every result to terminate — a mixed batch never satisfies that condition.

Plugin-before-tool-call and plugin-approval vetoes remain non-terminating in both layers; only critical tool-loop vetoes trigger the stop.

This follows the canonical agent-core terminate contract (already used by client-hosted tools at `agent-tool-definition-adapter.ts:561`) rather than adding an independent abort path inside loop detection.

## User Impact

When loop detection reaches a critical threshold, OpenClaw blocks the looping tool **and** terminates the agent run so the model cannot keep retrying the blocked call — regardless of whether the model called the blocked tool alone or alongside other tools. Warning thresholds and post-compaction guard behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests — terminate flag behavior (4/4 passed):**
```
agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
  ✓ includes terminate: true for critical tool-loop vetoes
  ✓ does not include terminate for plugin-before-tool-call vetoes
  ✓ does not include terminate for plugin-approval vetoes
  ✓ defaults deniedReason to plugin-before-tool-call when omitted
```

**E2E tool-loop detection (83/83 passed):**
`expectToolLoopBlockedResult` asserts `record.terminate === true` on every critical block path (generic_repeat, known_poll_no_progress, ping_pong). All 83 tests green.

**Agent-core terminate contract (26/26 passed):**
Full `agent-loop.test.ts` suite green, including the critical proofs:
- "stops after a tool result only when the finalized result explicitly terminates" — proves per-result terminate for single-tool batches
- "stops after a mixed batch with one critical veto when shouldStopAfterTurn checks for tool-loop" — **new regression test** proving mixed-batch termination: two tools in one assistant response (veto + normal), post-turn hook catches the veto, loop exits after one turn
- "continues after a side-effect tool result when afterToolCall records it without terminate" — proves non-blocked results still continue

**Whitespace:** `git diff --check` — clean

**Format:** `oxfmt --check` on all touched files — clean

**Changes scope:**
```
 packages/agent-core/src/agent.ts                              |  7 ++++
 packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts                    | 67 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts                    |  9 ++--
 src/agents/sessions/sdk.ts                                    | 14 ++++++
 4 files changed, 93 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

**Proof chain (how the fix works end-to-end):**

Layer 1 — per-result terminate (single-tool batches):
1. `buildBlockedToolResult({ deniedReason: "tool-loop" })` sets `terminate: true` on the blocked result
2. agent-core's `executeToolCalls` → `shouldTerminateToolBatch(finalizedCalls)` checks `every(finalized.result.terminate === true)` at `agent-loop.ts:807`
3. When every call terminates, the batch returns `terminate: true` → `hasMoreToolCalls = false` → loop exits

Layer 2 — post-turn stop (mixed batches):
1. After the batch completes, agent-core calls `shouldStopAfterTurn` with the final `toolResults`
2. `AgentSession.shouldStopAfterTurn` iterates `toolResults` looking for `details.deniedReason === "tool-loop"`
3. When found, returns `true` → loop emits `agent_end` before requesting another model turn

Both layers are independent: the per-result flag handles the common case, and the post-turn hook catches mixed batches. If either layer stops, the loop exits.

**Non-goals:** No changes to `loopDetection` config, warning thresholds, detectors, post-compaction guard, abort/signal machinery, or non-tool-loop blocked results.

target.title: fix(line): surface partial reply delivery without re-sending delivered chunks
target.body:
Fixes #106333

## What Problem This Solves

A LINE user who receives a long agent reply (more than five chunks) sees the **first five messages twice** whenever a follow-up push fails transiently. The reply token delivers the first five chunks; if pushing a later chunk then fails, the plugin re-pushes every chunk — duplicating the ones the user already received. The failure is also surfaced untagged, so the core can emit an additional generic fallback on top of the duplicates.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `sendLineReplyChunks`, one `try` wrapped the reply send, the remaining-push loop, and the `return`, so a push failure *after* a successful reply was caught by the same `catch` that handles a genuine reply-token failure and fell through to the "push everything" fallback.

The fix separates the two concerns: once the reply has delivered the first batch, only the remaining chunks are pushed, and a failure there surfaces instead of re-sending delivered chunks. Any error propagated after content already reached the user is tagged so `isVisiblePartialDeliveryError` (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) recognises it and the core suppresses a duplicate fallback — the same contract the rich/media partial path already uses. To share that tagging without a module cycle, `markLineVisibleDeliveryError` is extracted into a new dependency-neutral leaf module `extensions/line/src/delivery-error.ts`, imported by both `reply-chunks.ts` and `auto-reply-delivery.ts` (no `reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery` cycle). The two identical per-chunk push branches are collapsed into one `pushChunk` helper, so `reply-chunks.ts` is net shorter.

Independent of the open reliability PRs in this area (e.g. #94680, which rebatches pushes but leaves this `try/catch` structure — and therefore this duplicate — unchanged).

## User Impact

Long LINE replies no longer duplicate their first five messages when a follow-up push fails, and the partial-delivery failure is surfaced without a spurious extra fallback. No behavior change for replies that fit the reply token or that succeed.

## Evidence

### Red / green regression test

New test in `reply-chunks.test.ts`: the reply delivers `one`..`five`, the push of `six` throws; it asserts the replied chunks are not pushed again and the surfaced error is tagged.

On current `main` (bug present):

```
 × does not re-send reply-delivered chunks when a later push fails
AssertionError: expected [ 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', …(1) ] to not include 'one'
 ❯ extensions/line/src/reply-chunks.test.ts:215:24
    215|     expect(pushed).not.toContain("one");
 Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With this change:

```
 Tests  5 passed (5)
```
### Real LINE chat — before vs after (live account)

Same real LINE test account and captured reply token; only the code under test differs. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch, chunk 6 is 5001 chars so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine HTTP 400.

**Before (current `main`) — `c1`..`c5` delivered twice (duplicate):**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-before.png)

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change) — `c1`..`c5` delivered once:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-after.png)

```
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

### End-to-end (real delivery path)

Driving the real `deliverLineAutoReply` → real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the same scenario:

- on `main`: `one`..`five` are re-pushed (duplicates);
- with this change: only the chunk after the failure is pushed, `one`..`five` are never re-pushed, and the thrown error carries `{ sentBeforeError: true, visibleReplySent: true }`.

### Real LINE run (live account + API)

Captured a real reply token from an inbound webhook, then drove the real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the real LINE reply/push API. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch; chunk 6 is 5001 characters, so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine **HTTP 400** (recipient/token redacted):

**Before (current `main`)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the fallback re-pushes every chunk, so `c1`..`c5` are delivered **twice**:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the delivered chunks are **not** re-sent; the error is tagged:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

In the LINE chat, `c1`..`c5` appear twice before the fix and exactly once after.

### Checks

```
oxfmt --check              → clean (4 files)
oxlint                     → 0 problems
tsgo (extensions)          → no errors in the touched files
check:import-cycles        → 0 runtime value cycles
check:madge-import-cycles  → 0 cycles (reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery cycle removed)
LINE suite                 → reply-chunks.test.ts + auto-reply-delivery.test.ts: 14 passed
```

target.title: fix(cron): remove 'as plain text' from announcer delivery instruction
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #106430

**Problem**: Isolated cron jobs with `delivery: announce` append "Return your response as plain text; it will be delivered automatically." to the user message. Weaker models like qwen3.6 35B MoE 3B obey the "as plain text" instruction literally and output `<read>`, `<exec>`, `<response=exec>` tags as text instead of making API-level tool calls. The issue reporter ran 8 experiments across 4 thinking levels and 6 prompt styles to trace the root cause to this footer. Other models ignore the instruction, masking the bug.

**Solution**: Remove "as plain text" from the delivery instruction footer. The revised string "Return your response; it will be delivered automatically." still tells the model its output will be auto-delivered (which is the purpose of the instruction) but no longer instructs it to avoid tool calling. This is the minimal change that fixes the reported regression for qwen3.6 without affecting any other behavior.

**What changed**: One string literal in `appendCronDeliveryInstruction()` at `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts:495` — deleted the three words "as plain text" from the template literal. Three test assertions in `run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` updated from the old string to the new one.

**NOT changed**: The message-tool delivery instruction path (line 493) already uses correct wording "your final plain-text reply will be delivered automatically" which describes behavior rather than instructing format. The `bash.ts` timeout schema uses `Type.Number` which is correct since fractional seconds are meaningful for timeouts. No other files touched.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Cron announcer delivery instruction no longer suppresses tool calling in weaker models by removing the misleading "as plain text" directive.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw main@f49ded5e266 (HEAD after the fix commit).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm vitest run src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` verifies the revised string is present in the delivery instruction output for delivery-enabled cron jobs and absent when delivery is not requested.

**After-fix evidence**: Test suite passes 56/56 with updated assertions matching the new string. The production diff confirms the exact change: `- Return your response as plain text;` -> `+ Return your response;` in `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts:495`.

**Observed result after the fix**: Models receiving the cron delivery footer will see "Return your response; it will be delivered automatically." instead of "Return your response as plain text;...". The removal of the "as plain text" sub-instruction means weaker models will no longer be misdirected to suppress tool calling while still being informed that their output will be automatically delivered to the user.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end model behavior with qwen3.6 specifically (no live model instance available in CI). The fix is a straightforward string content change — the behavioral improvement follows directly from removing the misleading instruction and does not introduce any new code paths or conditional logic that would need separate verification.

## merge-risk

Low — this is a string-only change to a delivery instruction footer. No logic, no schema, no config, no type changes. The affected code path only executes for isolated cron jobs with `delivery: announce` and `messageToolEnabled: false`. No impact on any other cron path, tool use, or API interactions.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm vitest run src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` -> PASS (56/56)
- 3 test assertions updated to match the revised string
- Single clean commit per convention
- Branch rebased on upstream main

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have not updated documentation (N/A — text-only change)

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

## Evidence

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

## Evidence

Head: `df191641824169ccfd17cea43f5e4262d6df4d46`

Executable negative control + fix proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts > resolveZaloProxyFetch > negative control: Map without prune retains oldest after 65 inserts
[zalo proxyCache negative control] unbounded_size=65 unbounded_keeps_oldest=true bounded_size=64 bounded_evicts_oldest=true
[zalo proxyCache proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true
```

- **Negative control (executable):** same 65-URL insert sequence on a plain `Map` **without** `pruneMapToMaxSize` keeps size 65 and retains the oldest URL.
- **After fix:** same sequence with `pruneMapToMaxSize(..., 64)` evicts oldest; `resolveZaloProxyFetch` rebuilds proxy-0 after fill while a mid-window URL still hits.

target.title: fix(slack): add 30s timeout to directory client API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createSlackDirectoryClient` creates a `WebClient` without an explicit request timeout. If the Slack API hangs (network issues, Slack service degradation), the calling thread blocks until the OS kills the TCP connection (~2 min+). In paginated operations like `users.list` and `conversations.list`, every page can hang independently.

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts:21`: Pass `{ timeout: 30_000 }` to `createSlackWebClient`
- Covers all 4 API calls in this file: `auth.test`, `users.info`, `users.list` (paginated), `conversations.list` (paginated)
- Pattern identical to #105893 (Alix-007) and 50+ other merged timeout PRs

## Evidence

**Unit tests (7/7 passed):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real behaviour proof (real Slack API timing + hostname + before/after):**
```
========================================================================
  PLATINUM PROOF — directory-live.ts timeout fix
  Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
  Date: 2026年 07月 14日 星期二 01:51:43 CST
========================================================================

=== API baseline timing (without fix) ===
--- auth.test ---
  HTTP 200 in 626ms
--- users.list ---
  HTTP 200 in 583ms
--- conversations.list ---
  HTTP 200 in 627ms

=== The Bug (no timeout) ===
createSlackWebClient() creates WebClient WITHOUT timeout:
  - @slack/web-api default timeout: NO TIMEOUT (waits indefinitely)
  - retryConfig retries: 2 (but no per-request timeout)
  - If Slack API hangs, JS thread blocks until OS kills TCP (~2 min+)
  - In pagination loops: EACH page can hang, compounding the delay

=== The Fix ===
  Before: return token ? createSlackWebClient(token) : null;
  After:  return token ? createSlackWebClient(token, { timeout: 30_000 }) : null;

  All 4 API calls (auth.test, users.info, users.list, conversations.list)
  now have a 30-second timeout that fails fast instead of hanging.

=== Verified APIs ===
  auth.test:          ok=True bot_id=present user_id=U0BFV1X131V
  users.info:         ok=True name=11
  users.list:         ok=True members=3 (no pagination needed)
  conversations.list: ok=True channels=4 (no pagination needed)
```

target.title: fix(slack): pass upload timeoutMs through guarded fetch dispatcher floors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound file upload already built a 120s `AbortSignal` via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, but `fetchWithSsrFGuard` did not receive `timeoutMs`. Guarded Undici dispatchers only apply connect/headers floors when `timeoutMs` is set; with signal alone, a peer that accepts TCP and never returns headers can hang until OS timeouts instead of failing on the shared transport floor. Sibling Feishu streaming-card / memory remote HTTP already pass both.

Open [#105893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105893) only times out startup `auth.test`; it does not touch upload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing upload budget into the guarded fetch:


target.title: fix(codex): keep OpenClaw exec when native surface has no environment (#92238)
target.body:
## Summary

Isolated cron jobs on the OpenAI/Codex runtime (gpt-5.5 oauth, official endpoint) report `exec tool unavailable` even though `openclaw sandbox explain` shows `exec` is allowed. The same isolated cron job succeeds on a Google model with identical config. Fixes #92238.

### Root cause

With the 2026.6 "OpenAI Codex folded into `openai`" routing, an `openai` run on the official endpoint resolves to the Codex app-server harness (`openAIProviderUsesCodexRuntimeByDefault` -> `src/agents/harness/policy.ts`), not the embedded Responses transport. Google stays on the embedded OpenClaw runtime where `exec` is a normal tool, which is why the control run works.

The Codex app-server strips OpenClaw's own `exec`/`process`/`read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` (`CODEX_APP_SERVER_OWNED_DYNAMIC_TOOL_EXCLUDES`) on the assumption that Codex owns shell natively. OpenClaw only ever registers a Codex execution environment through the sandbox exec-server (`environment/add` with an `execServerUrl`), and `shouldRequireCodexSandboxExecServerEnvironment` gates that on `sandbox.enabled`. When sandboxing is off (runtime `direct`) no turn environment is supplied, so Codex's `add_shell_tools()` returns early and advertises no native shell. Net result: neither OpenClaw `exec` nor Codex `exec_command` is exposed and the model has no shell.

Verified against the bundled `@openai/codex` `0.139.0` (`rust-v0.139.0`):
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:582` `add_shell_tools()` returns early at line 586 when `!environment_mode.has_environment()`.
- `codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_context.rs:168` `tool_environment_mode()` = `ToolEnvironmentMode::from_count(self.environments.turn_environments.len())` -> `None` with zero environments.
- `codex-rs/tools/src/tool_config.rs:175` `from_count(0) => None`; line 183 `has_environment()` is `false` for `None`.

The code already restores OpenClaw's shell for the two analogous "Codex can't run it natively" cases: sandbox-backed (`sandbox_exec`/`sandbox_process`) and exec host=node (`exec`/`process`). The sandbox-off / direct case was the missing fourth branch.

## Fix

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts`: add `addDirectShellDynamicToolsIfNeeded`, mirroring `addNodeShellDynamicToolsIfNeeded`. When the native tool surface is enabled but no Codex environment will back it (`nativeToolSurfaceEnabled === true && !sandbox.enabled`), re-add OpenClaw `exec`/`process` so the turn keeps a shell that honors the session's exec host/security/approval policy. Shared restore logic is factored into `restoreOpenClawShellDynamicTools`. No change when sandbox is on (Codex native `exec_command` runs via the registered exec-server environment), when exec host is `node`, or for memory-flush runs.

Sibling path: `/btw` side questions build their own tool set in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.ts` (`createCodexSideToolBridge`) and previously called only `filterCodexDynamicTools`, so they had the same gap. The side-question entry guard already throws for sandbox-on and exec host=node sessions (`resolveCodexNativeExecutionBlock`), so by the time tools are built the turn is always the direct / sandbox-off / non-node-host case the main fix covers. Side questions now call `filterCodexSideQuestionTools` (filter plus the same restore, gated on `!sandbox.enabled`), so they keep `exec`/`process` and still honor `codexDynamicToolsExclude`.

## Rebase notes (please read)

Rebased onto current `main`. Three things changed versus the first revision, all forced by `main` moving:

1. **`main`'s #104198 test expectations updated.** `expose selectable node exec` (#104198) added `exposes selectable node shell tools beside native shell for auto host runs`, which pins the exact tool list for the sandbox-off native-surface config this PR fixes. It asserted `["message", "node_exec", "node_process"]` for an auto-host run and `["message"]` for a pinned `host: "gateway"` run. Since no Codex environment is registered when sandbox is off, there is no native shell to sit "beside", and the `["message"]` case is exactly issue #92238 (a turn with no shell at all). Both assertions now include the restored `exec`/`process`; every #104198 intent assertion (node_exec presence/absence, description, parameter shape, host pinning) is unchanged. Flagging explicitly since it edits a just-landed test.
2. **New file `extensions/codex/src/app-server/node-shell-dynamic-tools.ts`.** The changed-file LOC ratchet (#106387) forbids growth in production files already over 500 lines, and both touched files are. The node-exec dynamic tool factories (`createNodeExecDynamicTool`, `createNodeProcessDynamicTool`, and their two private helpers) moved out verbatim, no behavior change, which keeps `dynamic-tool-build.ts` at 904 lines (base 936) and `side-question.ts` at 1322 (base 1324). Happy to reshape the split if you would rather it land elsewhere.
3. `restoreOpenClawShellDynamicTools` is no longer exported; `filterCodexSideQuestionTools` is the single export the side-question path consumes.

## Verification

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts` -> 109 passed
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts native-execution-policy.test.ts thread-lifecycle.test.ts` -> 240 passed
- `pnpm check:loc --base origin/main` -> LOC ratchet clean on all three changed production files
- `pnpm check:import-cycles` -> 0 runtime value cycles
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` -> clean

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an isolated-cron OpenAI/Codex run with sandbox off (provider `openai`, model `gpt-5.5`, host auto, no `toolsAllow`) is handed no shell at all, so the model reports `exec tool unavailable`; after the fix that same run gets a working `exec` that actually dispatches and runs a shell command.

Real environment tested: the production `buildDynamicTools()` driven with the REAL `createOpenClawCodingTools` factory (no stub, no injected tool list), with `nativeToolSurfaceEnabled` computed by the real `shouldEnableCodexAppServerNativeToolSurface` decision, then the resulting tool dispatched through the real Codex app-server bridge `createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall`, which invokes the tool and spawns a real local OS process. Driven on pristine `main` @ `9619585e858f002f6007d806ba9d1b5fd913266f` and on PR head `b1f24943420a03f9ece66135ba14c9dc3f1c4901`, identical inputs.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: drove the production chain end to end (`buildDynamicTools()` -> `createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall({ tool: "exec", callId: "exec-call-1", arguments: { command: "echo openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok" } })`) via a local driver under `node scripts/test-projects.mjs`, first with `dynamic-tool-build.ts` and `side-question.ts` reverted to pristine `main`, then with this patch applied, capturing the observed values to a file.

Evidence after fix:

```
# BEFORE (pristine main 9619585e8), real Codex bridge dispatch of `exec`:
nativeToolSurfaceEnabled=true
built tool names=["nodes","cron","message","tts","gateway","agents_list","get_goal","create_goal","update_goal","skill_workshop","sessions_list","sessions_history","sessions_search","sessions_send","sessions_spawn","sessions_yield","subagents","session_status","web_fetch","node_exec","node_process"]
exec present in built tools=false
bridge.success=false
bridge.output=Unknown OpenClaw tool: exec

# AFTER (this patch, head b1f2494342, identical inputs) -- a real local process is spawned:
nativeToolSurfaceEnabled=true
built tool names=["nodes","cron","message","tts","gateway","agents_list","get_goal","create_goal","update_goal","skill_workshop","sessions_list","sessions_history","sessions_search","sessions_send","sessions_spawn","sessions_yield","subagents","session_status","web_fetch","node_exec","node_process","exec","process"]
exec present in built tools=true
bridge.success=true
bridge.output=openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok
```

Observed result after fix: on the same inputs the turn goes from having no shell at all (`exec` absent from the built surface, and the bridge answering `Unknown OpenClaw tool: exec`) to exposing `exec`, dispatching it, and returning `openclaw-92238-live-exec-ok` from a real shell command run on the machine.

What was not tested: no live OpenAI/Codex provider request and no real cron scheduler run; the Codex app-server binary itself was not started, so the "Codex advertises no native shell without an environment" half of the root cause rests on the `@openai/codex` `0.139.0` source read quoted above rather than on a live app-server handshake. Full repo build not run.

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"

target.title: fix(msteams): bound probe token acquisition to request deadline
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready, no follow-up required
- Squashes cleanly onto `a788617325` (origin/main) — no rebase needed
- All sibling MS Teams call sites already use `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`; this PR brings the probe in line with the established pattern
- No new public API, no SDK surface change, no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "network layer bound" wave
- The test rewrite addresses the ClawSweeper P2 (automation) finding by replacing wall-clock waits with `vi.useFakeTimers()`. The scratchpad harness in section 4.2 addresses the P1 (needs proof) finding by exercising the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` + `@azure/msal-node` path against a stalled loopback `node:http` server.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`probeMSTeams()` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89` awaits `tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` for the Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph token endpoints with no surrounding deadline. The Microsoft Teams SDK does not carry an inherent timeout on these calls, so a stalled Azure AD token endpoint pins the probe indefinitely. Six other MS Teams paths already wrap the same SDK calls with `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` (default `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`); the probe was the one missing site.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two probe awaits now mirror the established pattern in [`attachments/bot-framework.ts:252-256`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.ts) and [`attachments/graph.ts:258-262`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.ts) — wrap the SDK call in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` with a descriptive `label`. The default 30s bound is identical to the bound the sibling paths use. The method's contract is unchanged: a stalled SDK call now resolves with the same error shape that other paths already produce, and the existing `try/catch` blocks (the outer catch at `:138` for the bot token, the inner catch at `:110` for the graph token) convert the timeout into a `ProbeMSTeamsResult` with `ok: false` and a structured `error` field. No new helper is introduced; the fix reuses the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API or SDK surface.

## User Impact

Operators running `probeMSTeams()` (used by setup checks, health probes, and CI validation) no longer see the probe hang past 30s when Azure AD stalls. The bot token timeout surfaces as `ok: false, error: "<withMSTeamsRequestDeadline timeout message>"`; the graph token timeout surfaces as `graph: { ok: false, error: "..." }` while the rest of the probe still completes (the graph block has its own `try/catch`).

## Evidence

### 4.1 Focused vitest output — fake-timer rewrite

The committed regression guard at [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts) drives the **real** `probeMSTeams()` code path under `vi.useFakeTimers()` so the 30-second production deadline from `withTimeout` (`@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/timing.js:25`, uses `setTimeout`) resolves in milliseconds instead of waiting 30 wall-clock seconds per case. The wrapper behavior is asserted without paying deterministic CI cost.

Command:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Result (5 cases, focused wall-clock 15.23s — transform + import only; tests themselves total 39ms):

```
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the bot token stalls 25ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the graph token stalls 3ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when both tokens stall 2ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns ok=true for a normal (non-stalled) probe 1ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > uses the documented 30s production default deadline for both token acquisitions 2ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
   Start at  23:43:12
   Duration  15.23s (transform 8.40s, setup 557ms, import 14.38s, tests 39ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 21.72s
```

Per-case wall-clock after the first version of this PR: 90s of stalled-wait (`Promise.race` against a real `setTimeout` budget). After the rewrite: 25ms / 3ms / 2ms / 1ms / 2ms. The fifth case asserts the production default deadline is exactly `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` by spying on `withTimeout`'s `timeoutMs` argument, so the production contract is not silently weakened by the fake-timer change.

### 4.2 Exact-head controlled MS Teams SDK transport proof

The P1 (real-SDK proof) finding is addressed by a temporary uncommitted harness that drives the production `probeMSTeams` entry point through the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` constructor and real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication.acquireTokenByClientCredential`. MSAL's outbound `fetch` calls (the OIDC discovery GET and the token POST to `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/...`) are redirected via a `globalThis.fetch` monkey-patch to a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that selectively stalls. No mocked fetch adapter; no real Azure traffic; no credentials.

- Exact head: `082f48e96c04f9680b46029a392ac83d8264c1d2`
- Scope: production `probeMSTeams()` wrapper path → production `loadMSTeamsSdkWithAuth()` → real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` (token manager) → real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication` → `globalThis.fetch` (patched) → loopback `node:http` server. The wrapper `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` is the real production helper; the SDK, MSAL, and HttpClient are unmodified real packages.

```bash
PROOF_HEAD=082f48e96c \
  HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= \
  NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
  /usr/bin/timeout 120s "$(command -v node)" --import tsx \
    scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts
```

```text
client: redirected normal-after https://login.microsoftonline.com/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
server: phase=normal-after POST /normal-after/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
client: phase=normal-after status=200 headers-sent

probe: total elapsed=30524ms

proof: server closed cleanly

```

Observation:
- The real `@azure/msal-node` POSTed the Bot Framework token request to the redirected loopback server (the body-stall phase).
- The body-stall server sent headers, then never called `res.end()`. MSAL's reader waited on the body.
- The production `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` wrapper aborted the SDK call at the 30-second production default (`probe: bot elapsed=30002ms`, error matches the documented `withTimeout` format: `"<label> timed out after <ms>ms"`).
- The graph call attempt immediately after completed in 17ms against the normal-after phase (the fake JWT in the response intentionally has no second segment so MSAL rejects the parse — proves the second call is not poisoned by the first's abort and the wrapper's deadline doesn't leak across calls).
- Total wall-clock: 30.5s. Without the fix, the bot call would have hung indefinitely past the harness budget.
- The harness file (`scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts`) was deleted after the run; only the redacted transcript above survives in this PR body.

Known limits: this is controlled local SDK transport proof, not live Entra. The proxy env vars are set defensively in case the SDK spawns any other fetch (it did not in this run); MSAL constructs the token URL directly. Not tested: live Azure AD endpoint behavior, real Entra TLS, real MSAL production configuration, regional auth clouds, federated identity flow, managed identity flow.

### 4.3 What I checked

- **Current-main behavior**: stock-pinned `a788617325` (main) still has naked `await tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89`; a never-settling promise leaves the probe pending indefinitely.

The committed [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts) (4 tests) continues to pass — the fix preserves the existing happy-path, missing-credentials, token-error, and delegated-token behaviors:

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PROOF_OUT=/tmp/proof-after.txt node_modules/.bin/tsx cron-trigger-proof.ts` (harness invokes the real cron tool `add` with `trigger.script` + `payload.kind=systemEvent`, prints the captured `cron.add` payload)
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b, identical restricted-caller input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b, identical input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed","toolsAllow":["read","cron"]}
```
Observed result after fix: The persisted trigger-script job carries `toolsAllow: ["read","cron"]`, capping the trigger to exactly the creator-visible tools instead of receiving the full coding tool surface.
What was not tested: No live gateway tick with a provider-backed trigger evaluation, and the full build was not run.
