target.title: fix(memory-search): stop hybrid fusion from discounting vector-only multimodal results
target.body:
## Summary

Hybrid memory search ranks results with `finalScore = vectorWeight * vectorScore + textWeight * textScore`. `mergeHybridResults` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.ts`) applied that formula uniformly to every candidate. Image and audio chunks only carry a synthetic label as text, e.g. `Image file: media/IMG_0007.png` (`buildMemoryMultimodalLabel`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/multimodal.ts`). A natural-language query shares no words with that label, so a media chunk's BM25/text score is structurally near zero and it is seeded into the merge with `textScore: 0`. Under the default `0.7` vector / `0.3` text weights, a semantically strong media match is scaled to 70% of its vector score and ranks below a weaker text chunk that matches query keywords.

The fix makes fusion modality-aware. `mergeHybridResults` keeps the established weighted formula for every candidate, and only for a vector-only classified media chunk does it collapse the score to the vector signal:

```diff
-    const score = params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * entry.textScore;
+    const dropMediaTextSignal =
+      entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
+      params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
+      params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

For a non-text media chunk that has only a vector signal, dropping the near-zero text weight and renormalizing by the remaining vector weight collapses the score to its vector score, on the same `[0,1]` scale as text candidates. Every other candidate keeps the exact established weighted formula, so scoring scale, `minScore` filtering, and result ordering outside the vector-only media case are unchanged, including for custom weights that do not sum to one.

The manager supplies the predicate from the already-known file path, reusing the classifier the sync path uses (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`):

```ts
isNonTextMediaPath: (path) =>
  classifyMemoryMultimodalPath(path, this.settings.multimodal) !== null,
```

`classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` returns `null` when multimodal search is disabled, so the predicate is `false` for every path and behavior is identical to today on text-only setups. Modality is derived, not persisted, so there is no schema change or migration.

### Keyword-only media is preserved (review follow-up)

The first revision dropped the text weight for any media path. That zeroed a media chunk matched only by keyword (its label tokens) and no vector signal: `(0.7*0 + 0*text)/0.7 = 0`, dropping it from results. The merge now tracks an explicit `hasVector` flag per candidate and only drops the synthetic-label text signal when the candidate also has a vector signal. A keyword-only media hit keeps its normal text-weighted score, matching pre-fix behavior. Covered by a new regression test.

### Zero vector-weight configuration preserved (re-review follow-up)

`vectorWeight` may legitimately be `0` (existing memory tests run `{ vectorWeight: 0, textWeight: 1 }`). If a classified media chunk appeared in both the vector and keyword result sets, `hasVector` made the previous revision drop `textWeight`; `weightSum` then became `0 + 0` and the candidate scored `0`, suppressing a valid keyword match. The drop is also gated on a positive configured vector weight, so when `vectorWeight` is `0` the synthetic text signal is never the only meaningful signal and is kept. Covered by a regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1`.

### Both-signal media keeps its real keyword score (re-review follow-up)

Media labels are indexed and searchable (a manager test expects `search("image")`/`search("audio")` to find media). So a user who searches the label or filename can get the same media chunk back from FTS and from vector search at once. Gating the drop only on `hasVector` discarded the BM25/text score for that both-signal case, ignoring a real keyword match under positive `vectorWeight` and down-ranking a media file that legitimately matched FTS. The drop is now also gated on the candidate having no keyword signal, so the synthetic-label text weight is dropped only for genuinely vector-only media:

```diff
     const dropMediaTextSignal =
       entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
       params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
       params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
```

`hasKeyword` is tracked the same way as `hasVector`: it is set when a candidate is present in the keyword (FTS) result set. A vector-only media chunk (the #44540 case) still drops the synthetic label and scores on its vector signal; a media chunk with a real FTS hit now keeps the keyword contribution. Covered by a new regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight.

### Normalization limited to vector-only classified media (re-review follow-up)

An earlier revision computed `contentScore = weighted / weightSum` for every candidate. `weightSum` equals `1` only when the configured weights already sum to one; the public config exposes `vectorWeight` and `textWeight` independently, and existing tests run `{ vectorWeight: 1, textWeight: 1 }`. Under such a configuration the division halved the score of ordinary text and vector-only non-media candidates, which could change ordering and `minScore` filtering outside the reported bug. The renormalization is now applied only when `dropMediaTextSignal` is true; every other candidate retains the established unnormalized weighted formula exactly:

```diff
-    const effectiveTextWeight = dropMediaTextSignal ? 0 : params.textWeight;
-    const weightSum = params.vectorWeight + effectiveTextWeight;
-    const weighted =
-      params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + effectiveTextWeight * keywordScore;
-    const contentScore = weightSum > 0 ? weighted / weightSum : 0;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

Because `dropMediaTextSignal` is gated on `params.vectorWeight > 0`, collapsing the media score to `entry.vectorScore` is exactly `(vectorWeight * vectorScore) / vectorWeight` with no division by zero. Covered by two new regression tests, using `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (weights that do not sum to one): a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.

What is intentionally out of scope: persisting a modality column on chunks, and any change to the text-only ranking path.

### Rebase onto current main and the TypeScript LOC ratchet

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet on `main` forbids an oversized legacy file from growing, and `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` is already 1671 lines, so plumbing the media predicate into the merge call tripped the gate. The merge wrapper's inline parameter type moved to `hybrid.ts`, which owns the merge contract, and is referenced as `ManagerHybridMergeParams`. `manager.ts` now shrinks to 1660 lines. The modality-aware fusion fix is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: hybrid fusion discounted a vector-only image match by the configured text weight, so a semantically strong media result ranked below a weaker keyword-matching text note.
Real environment tested: the real production memory retrieval path driven on pristine `main` (`1708faf85b`) and on PR head `c02d11dc7f` with identical inputs: a real `node:sqlite` memory index built with the production `ensureMemoryIndexSchema`, a real FTS5 index scored by the production `searchKeyword` with real BM25 ranking, the real `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` modality classifier wired exactly as `MemoryIndexManager` wires it, and the real `mergeHybridResults` fusion under the default `vectorWeight 0.7, textWeight 0.3`. The corpus is one image file, one keyword-matching note, and 18 filler documents so BM25 has real IDF.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: indexed the corpus, ran the query `underwater coral reef survey` through the production keyword search and hybrid fusion, then reverted only `hybrid.ts` to its pristine `main` contents and re-ran the identical scenario.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b)
query: underwater coral reef survey
fusion weights: vectorWeight=0.7 textWeight=0.3
classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/media/IMG_0007.png") -> image
classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/field-notes.md") -> null
ranked memory search results:
  #1  score=0.9376  vector=0.9487  bm25=0.9116  memory/field-notes.md
  #2  score=0.7000  vector=1.0000  bm25=0.0000  memory/media/IMG_0007.png
top result: memory/field-notes.md

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head c02d11dc7f)
query: underwater coral reef survey
fusion weights: vectorWeight=0.7 textWeight=0.3
classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/media/IMG_0007.png") -> image
classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/field-notes.md") -> null
ranked memory search results:
  #1  score=1.0000  vector=1.0000  bm25=0.0000  memory/media/IMG_0007.png
  #2  score=0.9376  vector=0.9487  bm25=0.9116  memory/field-notes.md
top result: memory/media/IMG_0007.png
```
Observed result after fix: the image chunk carries a strong vector signal (1.0000) but a structurally zero BM25 signal, because its only indexed text is the synthetic `Image file:` label. Before the patch the 0.3 text weight scaled it down to 0.7000 and it lost to the weaker note at 0.9376. After the patch it scores on its vector signal (1.0000) and surfaces first, while the note keeps its identical 0.9376 score, so the ranking flips to put the strongest semantic match on top.
What was not tested: no live embedding provider request was made, so the query and chunk vectors are deterministic local values rather than Gemini-served embeddings; the approximate-nearest-neighbour vector index lookup was not exercised, and the vector scores were supplied directly to fusion. Everything else on the retrieval path (schema, FTS5, BM25 ranking, modality classification, fusion) is the real production code. A full production build was not run.

## Verification

- Real before/after through the production memory retrieval path above (real `node:sqlite` schema, FTS5/BM25 keyword search, real modality classifier, real fusion), pristine `main` vs this patch on identical inputs.
- Regression coverage in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts`: vector-only media scored on its vector signal without the text-weight discount; text-candidate scoring unchanged when a media predicate is supplied; keyword-only media preserved (not dropped to zero); a classified media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1` keeps its keyword score; a classified media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight keeps its keyword score instead of being discounted; and, under `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1`, a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts` (22 passed).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search.test.ts` (34 passed).

Closes #44540

target.title: fix(clickclack): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClickClack realtime websocket creation set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `gateway.ts` waits on `close`/`error`/`abort` after `client.websocket(...)`; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends and the monitor reconnect loop is pinned. Slack relay, Mattermost, and Signal already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Bake `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` into `createClickClackClient().websocket()` via `CLICKCLACK_WEBSOCKET_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- Timeout-induced `error`/`close` already returns control to the existing reconnect loop — no gateway.ts logic change.
- Regressions assert source wiring and prove a real TCP hang fails at ~30s.

No new config/env surface.

Note: open [#104006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104006) adds REST request timeouts in the same client file and intentionally leaves WS alone; this PR is the WS follow-up and should rebase cleanly after that lands.

## User Impact

**Before:** A ClickClack realtime peer that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel monitor forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` / close 1006), allowing the monitor to reconnect.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts`
- Production caller: `gateway.ts` → `client.websocket(...)`
- Sibling: Slack relay / Mattermost / Signal `handshakeTimeout: 30_000`
- Regression: `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ delivers a legitimate inbound frame below the payload cap
 ✓ delivers a valid event frame above the server request-body limit
 ✓ rejects an oversized inbound frame before it reaches the event parser
 ✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost
[clickclack handshake live proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=30010 handshakeTimeout_ms=30000 error=Opening handshake has timed out
 ✓ returns when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade 30012ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**Before fix:**
`websocket()` options had no `handshakeTimeout`, so a TCP peer that never upgraded could leave `gateway.ts` waiting forever for `close`/`error`.

**After fix:**
Production client wires `handshakeTimeout: 30000`. Against a TCP peer that accepts but never upgrades, real `ws` fails at ~30s.

**Evidence after fix:**
```text
[clickclack handshake live proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=30010 handshakeTimeout_ms=30000 error=Opening handshake has timed out
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

**What was not tested:**
Live ClickClack credentials; full gateway packaging beyond the production `ws` client options used by `gateway.ts`. REST request timeouts remain covered by [#104006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104006).

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

## Evidence

Head: `df191641824169ccfd17cea43f5e4262d6df4d46`

Executable negative control + fix proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts > resolveZaloProxyFetch > negative control: Map without prune retains oldest after 65 inserts
[zalo proxyCache negative control] unbounded_size=65 unbounded_keeps_oldest=true bounded_size=64 bounded_evicts_oldest=true
[zalo proxyCache proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true
 ✓ |extension-zalo| extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts > resolveZaloProxyFetch > negative control: Map without prune retains oldest after 65 inserts 3ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Negative control (executable):** same 65-URL insert sequence on a plain `Map` **without** `pruneMapToMaxSize` keeps size 65 and retains the oldest URL.
- **After fix:** same sequence with `pruneMapToMaxSize(..., 64)` evicts oldest; `resolveZaloProxyFetch` rebuilds proxy-0 after fill while a mid-window URL still hits.
- Touched: `extensions/zalo/src/proxy.ts` (+ colocated test). Sibling Nextcloud/MS Teams/Mattermost prune callers unchanged.

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 4 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:list` — completed.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — passed (705 files).
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Repository autoreview against `origin/main` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Remote `check:changed` could not start: Blacksmith is not authenticated in this environment, and the configured AWS Crabbox broker is unavailable. PR CI remains the broader validation path.

### Redacted live completion-wake proof

- Restarted Gateway source build: `88927b2c63b866fce554faeafea422ba7ed3cc21`, the deployment backport of PR head `5e0b5a055c05f74854a2f0d9f9c7c3b146c7ad7a`.
- Deep Gateway RPC and health probes passed; the event loop was not degraded.
- A model-facing `create_goal` call established an active goal on a durable user-facing owner session.
- The live session projection confirmed that the runtime policy session key was present and differed from the durable owner session key. Values are intentionally omitted.
- A completion event was queued through the supported Gateway wake path for that durable owner.
- The resulting embedded production turn called `get_goal`; the authoritative tool payload returned `status: found` with the same active objective.
- The same wake turn called `update_goal({ status: "complete" })`; the authoritative tool payload returned `status: updated` with goal status `complete`.
- A fresh persisted-state read confirmed that the goal remained on the durable owner and was `complete`; no goal was written to the policy session.
- Post-proof health remained healthy; the temporary proof goal and scoped attach grant were removed/revoked.

This evidence intentionally omits all session keys, goal IDs, chat/group/topic/message IDs, usernames, account IDs, tokens, filesystem paths, connection IDs, run IDs, and trace IDs.

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu inbound media downloads that stall after the Lark SDK returns a stream body (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `saveMessageResourceFeishu` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that attachment.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route every Feishu inbound `saveMediaStream` path through `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` (production floor 30s), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the WhatsApp/LINE channel pattern.
- Idle helper lives in `extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.ts` so the oversized legacy `media.ts` does not grow past the LOC ratchet.
- On timeout, reject with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()`, and silence the losing `next()`.
- Only `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` is exported (knip); timeout class/helper stay module-private.
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts`.
- Does **not** touch Feishu docx URL reads (`#104663`).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Feishu message-resource body could hang inbound handling for that attachment indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the Feishu monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `6b965bbf7b143876d09fe7487c541076d0f90644`

Executable negative control + fix proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts > saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout > negative control: never-yielding stream without idle wrap stays pending
[feishu media idle negative control] outcome=still-pending wait_ms=150 without_idle_wrap=true
[feishu media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=51 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000
 ✓ |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts > saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout > negative control: never-yielding stream without idle wrap stays pending 156ms
[feishu media idle proof] production_default_ms=30000 timed_out=true

```

- **Negative control (executable):** same never-yielding AsyncIterable consumed with bare `for await` (no idle wrap) stays `still-pending` after 150ms.
- **After fix:** `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` with 50ms floor rejects promptly; production default advances fake timers to 30s; `iterator.return()` called once on timeout.
- Touched: `extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.ts` + `media.ts` call sites (LOC-neutral helper extract). Sibling WhatsApp/LINE idle floors unchanged (different owners).

target.title: fix(line): cap user profile cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded in-process `userProfileCache` in the LINE send path (`extensions/line/src/send.ts`). Profile lookups are cached for 5 minutes (TTL) but had no entry-count cap, so gateways serving many distinct LINE users accumulate Map entries indefinitely until process restart.

**Concrete scenario:** A LINE gateway processing inbound messages from 10 000 distinct users over several hours caches each `getUserProfile` result. With no size cap, the cache grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 1 024-entry cap via the existing `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`, matching Slack / Discord / Nextcloud Talk channel caches.

`touchLineUserProfileCache` deletes + sets so Map insertion order refreshes on both write and TTL-valid read hits (same LRU-on-access pattern as `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`). Active users stay under the cap; idle oldest-inserted entries evict first.

No config/env knobs. TTL behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-lived LINE gateways accumulate one `userProfileCache` entry per distinct user indefinitely.

**After:** Cache stays at ≤ 1 024 entries. Recently touched profiles survive eviction; untouched oldest entries are pruned. First 1 024 distinct users behave as before until the cap is exceeded.

## Evidence

- `extensions/line/src/send.ts` — `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`, `touchLineUserProfileCache` (delete + set + `pruneMapToMaxSize`) on write and TTL hit
- `extensions/line/src/monitor.ts` — inbound path calls `getUserDisplayName` → `getUserProfile`
- Sibling pattern: `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts` (`getCachedSlackConversationInfo` / `setCachedSlackConversationInfo`)
- Shared helper: `src/infra/map-size.ts` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` (`pruneMapToMaxSize`)
- Regression: `extensions/line/src/send.test.ts`
  - eviction past cap via `getUserDisplayName`
  - recently touched entry retained under cap

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/send.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > caches profile results by default 0ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > evicts oldest profile cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 8ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > keeps recently touched profile entries under the cache cap 9ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.64s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** LINE user-profile Map no longer grows without bound; active entries refresh insertion order so they survive pruning.
- **Canonical reachability path:**

```text
LINE inbound webhook (monitor)
  → getUserDisplayName(userId)
  → getUserProfile(userId)
  → touchLineUserProfileCache (delete + set)
  → pruneMapToMaxSize(userProfileCache, 1024)
```

- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production `getUserDisplayName` / `getUserProfile` / `touchLineUserProfileCache` through the real unmocked `pruneMapToMaxSize` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`. Only `@line/bot-sdk` `MessagingApiClient.getProfile` is stubbed (no live LINE credentials in this environment). There is no DI seam for the Messaging API client; production constructs `new messagingApi.MessagingApiClient(...)` inside `createLineMessagingClient`.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Cap and LRU-on-access match Slack conversation-info and other channel `pruneMapToMaxSize` caches. No new config/env surface.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2, branch `fix/line-cap-user-profile-cache` rebased onto `upstream/main` (head `72708ef81051498a04177d33a5e57dc21903b3ec`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/send.test.ts --reporter=verbose

# Standalone production-path proof (real send.ts cache + real pruneMapToMaxSize;
# only MessagingApiClient.getProfile stubbed via Node module loader):
OPENCLAW_ROOT=/tmp/openclaw-pr-fixes/101741 \
  node --import tsx \
  --import /tmp/line-user-profile-cache-proof/register-line-bot-sdk-stub.mjs \
  /tmp/line-user-profile-cache-proof/line-user-profile-cache-proof.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix (Vitest):**

```text
 ✓ caches profile results by default
 ✓ evicts oldest profile cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 8ms
 ✓ keeps recently touched profile entries under the cache cap 9ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

- **Evidence after fix (standalone, non-Vitest production path):**

```text
{"proof":"line-user-profile-cache-cap","root":"/tmp/openclaw-pr-fixes/101741","boundary":"@line/bot-sdk MessagingApiClient.getProfile stub only","production":["getUserDisplayName","getUserProfile","touchLineUserProfileCache","pruneMapToMaxSize"],"liveLineGateway":false}
{"step":"eviction","ok":true,"detail":"U-first evicted after 1024 newer inserts; refetch required"}
{"step":"lru-retention","ok":true,"detail":"U-keep survived prune after touch; U-fill-1 evicted"}
{"RESULT":"pass","liveLineGateway":false}
```

Regression flow (caller path `getUserDisplayName`):

1. Resolve `U-first` → 1 API call, cached
2. Resolve `U-fill-1` … `U-fill-1024` → 1 024 more API calls; `U-first` evicted at cap
3. Resolve `U-first` again → 1 API call (eviction proven)

LRU retention flow:

1. Fill cache to 1 024 including `U-keep`
2. Touch `U-keep` (0 extra API calls; insertion order refreshed)
3. Insert `U-new` → oldest untouched (`U-fill-1`) evicted; `U-keep` still cached (0 API calls)

- **What was not tested:** Live LINE gateway / Messaging API with real channel access tokens. No redacted live LINE webhook transcript under sustained distinct-user traffic. Optional supplemental proof: gateway log showing cache size stabilizing at ≤ 1 024 under real LINE inbound load.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

target.title: fix(agents): preserve ANSI sanitizer state across bash chunks
target.body:
Closes #103668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running bash commands through agents could see ANSI/OSC control-sequence fragments leak into streamed tool output, final bash results, and full-output spill files when a process split a terminal sequence across output callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a reusable incremental ANSI sequence stripper in terminal-core and lets the bash output accumulator use one sanitizer instance for the lifetime of each command. This preserves streaming and bounded-memory behavior while keeping one-shot `stripAnsiSequences()` semantics unchanged for existing callers.

## User Impact

Bash output sanitization is now invariant to callback chunking for OSC and CSI sequences. Agents and users receive the same clean output whether the process emits a complete sequence in one callback or splits it across callbacks.

## Evidence

Before this patch, sanitizing `A\x1b]0;title` and `\x07B` independently leaked fragments such as `Aitle\x07B`; whole-input sanitization returned `AB`.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): keep export tree truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The exported session HTML tree preview must truncate long node text without breaking emoji or other supplementary-plane characters, and it must not scan or allocate the entire message just to keep the first 100 preview characters. The first code-point-safe implementation used `Array.from(s)` over the full message text, which could make large session exports stall or allocate heavily.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up replaces full-string materialization with a bounded `for...of` scan that stops at the preview budget and slices by the resulting UTF-16 offset. This preserves code-point-safe truncation and the existing `...` suffix while avoiding full traversal/allocation of large message content.

## User Impact

`/export-session` HTML tree previews keep emoji boundaries intact and remain responsive when a session contains very large message text.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head after bot follow-up: `2c85cc6104a`
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.js src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.js src/auto-reply/reply/export-html/template.security.test.ts`: no formatting target because these export-html files are ignored by oxfmt in this checkout, not a formatting failure
- Real-browser proof: generated a session export HTML with a tree message shaped as `99 x chars + U+1F600 + 500000 y chars`, opened the generated file in headless system Chrome through Playwright, and captured `.tree-content` from the rendered page:

```json
{
  "text": "user: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx??...",
  "codePoints": 109,
  "containsEmoji": true,
  "emojiHex": "1f600",
  "containsEllipsisSuffix": true,
```

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ ... > openStream > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Production-path connect-timeout storm proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The storm case runs production `openStream` → `urbitFetch` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against a real loopback `node:http` server that returns `503` five times; real timers; each armed `setTimeout(..., 60000)` is cleared. The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers, including under repeated failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` + closed-port TCP failure; production SSRF-guarded transport (no `urbitFetch` mock, no fake timers).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Same `try/finally { clearTimeout }` pattern as `extensions/zalouser/src/probe.ts`; no new config/API.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners and real timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.open-stream-timeout.proof.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when urbitFetch rejects 12ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timeout when the stream response is not ok 10ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears connect timers after a real non-OK stream response storm 305ms
 ✓ |extension-messaging| ... > clears the connect timer when production urbitFetch rejects 10ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 7.90s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Five sequential non-OK connects each arm then clear a 60s connect timer with matching `clearTimeout(handle)`; a real transport reject also clears its single connect timer.
- **What was not tested:** Live Urbit ship reconnect storm against a real Tlon host; SSE stream body processing after a successful connect.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Successful connects still clear the timer after headers; only failed connects gain the missing cleanup.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(restart): keep deferring when pending inspection fails
target.body:
Fixes #104064.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart deferral treated pending-work inspection exceptions as proof that the gateway was idle. That fail-open path could restart while active work still existed but could not be inspected. The first patch fixed the helper retry behavior, but the config-reload caller still cleared its restartPending guard from onCheckError even though the helper now keeps polling. A later config change could therefore start duplicate deferral loops and competing restart preparation.

## Summary

- Treat pending-count inspection exceptions as unknown pending work instead of safe-to-restart.
- Keep the existing deferral lifecycle active after both initial and later getPendingCount failures.
- Preserve the config-reload restartPending guard when retrying inspection failures.
- Update the production warning to say the deferral is waiting and retrying instead of restarting immediately.
- Continue polling until a later check confirms idle, or until the explicit maxWaitMs timeout forces the existing timeout path.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation on 422023a5d715b3833c1683df674ae6b57662e4a7:

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed; 2 shards, 107 tests.
- node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.non-agents.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-non-agents.tsbuildinfo -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.deferral-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts -> passed.
- pnpm check:loc --base upstream/main --head HEAD -> passed.
- git diff --check -> passed.

Focused behavior covered:

- Initial pending inspection throw calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Later polling throw calls onCheckError, keeps polling, and later emits only after a successful idle check.
- Config-reload caller keeps restartPending active after an inspection error; a later config restart request does not create duplicate restart emission work.

## Root Cause

The helper and its production caller disagreed about onCheckError semantics. The helper now treats inspection failure as non-terminal, so the caller must keep its deferral guard active until ready, timeout, cancel, or emission settlement.

## Behavior After This Patch

- Initial inspection throw: calls onCheckError, enters deferral with pending=1, and polls again.
- Later polling throw: calls onCheckError, keeps the interval registered, and retries on the next poll.
- Config reload inspection throw: keeps restartPending true and logs waiting/retrying.
- Confirmed pending=0 still emits restart through the normal ready path.
- Explicit maxWaitMs still preserves the existing forced-timeout behavior.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to media-bearing replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3), branch `fix/bug-001-accumulatedText-empty-replace`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  35 passed (35)
  ```

  Focused regression tests:
  ```
  ✓ preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
  ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
  ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
  ```

- **Shared code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check. The runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets.

- **Observed result after fix**: Media-bearing empty-text replacement preserves accumulated assistant text ("Lime green apple") instead of clearing it to "No response from OpenClaw."
- **What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Real multimodal provider E2E flow (the event shape is produced by the agent runtime, not the provider directly; the mock test exercises the exact runtime event sequence).

### Real behavior proof

The fix was verified with a guard condition proof simulating 6 event shapes:

```
Event shape                                | main (bug)      | PR (fixed)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Empty text + valid mediaUrls             | REPLACE (bug!)  | PRESERVE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrls:[]                | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrl:''                 | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Non-empty text (normal replacement)      | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
```

The guard condition:
```
main guard:  replace && typeof text === "string"
           = true → accumulatedText = "" ✗ BUG

PR guard:   replace && typeof text === "string" && (text || !hasMediaContent)
           = true && ("" || !true) → false → accumulatedText PRESERVED ✓
```

The agent runtime producer code proves that `{ text: "", replace: true, mediaUrls: [...] }` is always a media-only addition, never an intentional text deletion.

### Regression test plan

3 regression tests cover the behavioral surface:
1. Valid `mediaUrls` → text preserved
2. Empty `mediaUrls: []` → text cleared (existing behavior)
3. Empty `mediaUrl: ""` → text cleared (existing behavior)

All 35 gateway tests pass with zero regression.

target.title: feat(ui): redesign Channels page with guided channel setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Settings → Channels page was a wall of raw schema-driven config forms — every channel rendered every field (tokens, allowlists, JSON blobs) inline, with no guidance on how to actually connect a channel. A beginner landing on the page had no path from "I want OpenClaw on Telegram" to a working bot: the real setup knowledge (BotFather, Slack manifests, WhatsApp QR pairing) only existed in the CLI wizard (`openclaw channels add`) and the docs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebuilds Channels in the unified settings design language (#106470) and adds a guided, step-by-step setup wizard to the web UI — without duplicating any setup logic:

- **Gateway (additive protocol):** `wizard.start` gains `flow: "channels"` + `channel` params, routing to the shared channel-setup flow (`openclaw channels add`) over the existing `WizardSession` step protocol already used by the macOS/Android onboarding clients. The wizard branch of `channelsAddCommand` is extracted into a prompter-injectable runner (`src/commands/channels/add-wizard.ts`); the gateway entry never calls `runtime.exit`. On completion the runner reports the channels it actually configured, surfaced as an additive `channels` field on the terminal `wizard.next` result so the client keys channel-specific completion off the real outcome, not the preselection.
- **`SetupChannelsOptions.deferDeviceLinkToClient`:** gateway clients render device linking natively, so the WhatsApp finalize surface skips its terminal QR login; the Control UI runs QR pairing through the existing `web.login.start/wait` RPCs instead.
- **Control UI:** the page becomes "Your channels" (settings-language rows with 44px art tiles and dot statuses: Running / Configured / Needs attention) + "Add a channel" (guided-setup rows incl. a browse-all entry that reaches npm-installable catalog channels), following the unified settings design language (uppercase section headings, one flat group surface, hairline rows, status dots). A detail overlay keeps the full advanced surface: the migrated per-channel settings sections with live status facts, start/relink/logout actions, and the complete schema config form. The wizard modal renders the generic step vocabulary (select / multiselect / text-with-masking / confirm / note with copy button) plus per-channel helper links (BotFather, Discord developer portal, api.slack.com/apps, docs.openclaw.ai) and finishes WhatsApp setup with an embedded QR pairing phase.
- Config writes from the wizard hot-reload channels via the existing chokidar config watcher; no restart needed.

Row/cover art reuses the bundled `plugin-art` set (CSP is `img-src 'self'`, so remote brand icons can't load). The mock-dev harness gains channels/wizard fixtures so the flow is demoable and screenshot-testable offline.

## User Impact

Setting up a channel is now: open Channels → click a card → follow 2–4 short steps → done (WhatsApp ends with a scannable QR right in the dialog). All ~20 channels with setup surfaces work through the same wizard automatically, and everything that was on the old page (full config form, status detail, health JSON) is still there behind the card detail view. CLI behavior is unchanged; the macOS/Android wizard clients are unaffected (protocol change is additive).

target.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw parses `openclaw.json` using JSON5, which supports comments. However, when the configuration is modified, the system saves back using standard `JSON.stringify()`, which strips all user-authored comments.

**Issue**: #105683

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `src/config/io.ts` where config writes use `JSON.stringify()` which cannot preserve JSON5 comments.

This PR implements a warning to notify users when their comments will be lost. The warning is **not** gated on `skipOutputLogs` — comment stripping is a data-loss event that should always be surfaced, even for machine-parseable (`--json`) callers.

## User Impact

### Before
- Users add comments to `openclaw.json` for documentation
- Any config modification silently strips all comments

### After  
- Users receive a clear warning when writing config with JSON5 comments
- The warning fires regardless of output mode (including `--json` / `skipOutputLogs`)
- The warning intelligently excludes false positives (URLs in strings)

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`), but the blocked result was returned to the model as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

Abort the embedded attempt at the run owner boundary when a tool result is a critical tool-loop block. One typed helper owns the contract; direct-tool wraps, Tool Search hydration wraps, and Tool Search target execution all call it.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the run instead of burning resources indefinitely.
- Non-loop blocks (plugin/approval vetoes) are unchanged.
- Operators see a terminated run rather than a zombie session after `action=block` at critical level.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `c46f9dc8dfcec464c5d92df79b76d0b8ce034e4f` (rebased onto current `main`)

### Rank-up coverage

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Rebase onto current main | done |
| One typed critical-loop termination helper | `critical-tool-loop-abort.ts` |
| Invoke from direct-tool + Tool Search paths | 3 call sites in `attempt.ts` |
| Focused regression for both paths | 4 tests in `critical-tool-loop-abort.test.ts` |
| No subsequent provider turn after critical block | unit loop transcript below (`provider-turn` then `abort` only) |

### Patch shape

- 3 files: helper + test + `attempt.ts` wiring (~+10 on attempt; helper/tests focused)
- No speculative public exports beyond the run-local helper
- Explicit contract: `status === "blocked" && deniedReason === "tool-loop"` (not bare string heuristic)

### L1 / whole-path helper proof (production helper on the call chain)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/critical-tool-loop-abort.test.ts --reporter=verbose

✓ |agents| src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/critical-tool-loop-abort.test.ts > critical tool-loop abort helper > recognizes only blocked tool-loop results 76ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/critical-tool-loop-abort.test.ts > critical tool-loop abort helper > aborts for a direct-tool critical loop and leaves no room for a follow-up provider turn 5ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
   Duration  583ms (transform 351ms, setup 266ms, import 34ms, tests 87ms, environment 0ms)
```

Direct-tool and Tool Search simulated agent loops both emit exactly:
`["provider-turn", "abort"]` — no second provider turn after the critical block.

### Before / after

|---|---|---|

| Critical `tool-loop` on Tool Search hydrated tool | same zombie loop | same abort via `captureAbortRun` |

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which clones and sorts the full task registry. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work blocks the event loop, causing gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of repeating per-row task scans, a batch snapshot collects all session keys with pending generated-media work in one pass:

1. **`buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet()`** — one-time scan over task registry + in-process activity map, returns `Set<string>`
2. **Lazy initialization** — snapshot is built only when the first `cronRunContinuation` row is encountered. Idle sweeps (deployments with no cron jobs) pay zero cost and have no task-store failure dependency.
3. **O(1) lookup** — `Set.has()` inside the loop replaces O(T) scan per row

The snapshot preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change.

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes
- **Tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 9 tests (+6 for `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet`)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests (mock updated, pending-media tests use `buildPendingSet`)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −5 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys()`
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet()`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — lazy snapshot + O(1) lookup
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface

- **Performance:** O(S × T) → O(T + S), real simulation shows 27.2x speedup at 500 sessions × 1000 tasks:

```
[Case 2] Performance scaling — O(S×T) vs O(T+S)
  scale: 500 sessions × 1000 tasks
  old: 13.6ms — 500 full task-list scans (clone+sort each)
  new: 0.5ms — 1 full task-list scan + 500 Set.has() lookups
  speedup: 27.2x
  real clone cost: old=500,000 element copies → new=1,000 element copies
```

- **Real gateway log output** — production `sweepCronRunSessions` with gateway pino-style log:

```
[gateway] INFO  cron-reaper: pruned 2 expired cron run session(s)  {"pruned":2,"retentionMs":86400000}
```

The proof seeds 5 sessions (3 cron run, 2 expired) into a real session store, runs the reaper at `force: true`, and captures the same log format a production gateway emits. After pruning, only the base + recent + regular sessions remain. A second sweep correctly produces no log (pruned=0).

- **Lazy snapshot contract:**
  - 0 continuations → 0 task registry scans (idle sweep fast path)
  - 1+ continuations → 1 scan, all rows use `Set.has()`
  - Test: 5 continuations → 0 per-row `hasPending` calls, batch set populated once

- **[P2] Idle sweep regression fixed** — snapshot is `??=` initialized on first continuation row:

```typescript
let pendingMediaSessionKeys: Set<string> | undefined;
for (const { sessionKey, entry } of listSessionEntries({ storePath })) {
  // ... non-cron-run skip, non-continuation expiry ...
  const continuation = entry.cronRunContinuation;
  if (continuation) {
    pendingMediaSessionKeys ??= buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet();
    if (pendingMediaSessionKeys.has(sessionKey)) continue;
  }
  // ... prune logic ...
}
```

target.title: fix(signal): bound container receive websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container receive streaming created the long-lived `/v1/receive` WebSocket with `maxPayload` but no `handshakeTimeout`. `streamContainerEvents` waits for the connection lifecycle (`open` / `close`); when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends, so `runSignalSseLoop` cannot reconnect. The probe path in the same file already times out; only the long-lived receive path was missing a hang floor. Slack relay and Mattermost already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildSignalContainerWebSocketOptions` as the single production options surface (`maxPayload` + `handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Probe and long-lived receive both consume that builder.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control from `streamContainerEvents`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Signal container that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the receive reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` / close), allowing `runSignalSseLoop` to continue reconnecting.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts`
- Production caller: `streamContainerEvents` → `streamSignalEvents` → `runSignalSseLoop`
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`); Mattermost `#105553`
- Asymmetry proof: same-file probe already timed out; long-lived receive did not
- Regression: `extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts`, `extensions/signal/src/client-container.ws-handshake.test.ts`

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.ws-handshake.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

target.title: fix(vault): bound Vault SecretRef JSON response reads to 1 MiB
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded `response.json()` read in the Vault SecretRef resolver that allows a hostile or misconfigured Vault endpoint to OOM the resolver process by streaming an arbitrarily large JSON body.

`vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` calls `await response.json()` on two success paths — the JWT/Kubernetes login response (line 206) and the KV secret read response (line 245) — without any body-size cap. The resolver validates `VAULT_ADDR` origin and enforces a 5-second fetch timeout, but neither prevents a slow-streaming multi-MiB response body from being fully buffered in memory. Vault KV payloads and auth tokens are inherently tiny (< 1 KB), so any response approaching 1 MiB is anomalous.

Sibling bounded-response campaign PRs: #103908, #103757, and others already fixed this pattern across provider extensions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a local `readJsonWithLimit` helper (1 MiB cap) that streams `response.body` chunk-by-chunk, cancels the reader and throws if the total byte count exceeds the limit, then assembles and JSON-parses the bounded buffer. This file is a standalone Node.js script with a test-enforced constraint against importing from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, so the bounded reader is implemented inline using only Node.js Fetch API built-ins (`ReadableStream`, `TextDecoder`).

Both `await response.json()` calls on the success path are replaced with `await readJsonWithLimit(response)`.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hostile or misconfigured Vault endpoint returning an oversized JSON body (e.g. 24 MiB) causes the resolver process to buffer the entire body before erroring or parsing, risking OOM on agents that resolve many secrets concurrently.

**After:** The resolver cancels the response stream and returns a per-id error (`Vault response body exceeds 1048576-byte limit`) once body bytes cross 1 MiB. Normal Vault KV and auth responses (< 1 KB) are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` — adds `VAULT_JSON_RESPONSE_LIMIT_BYTES` constant + `readJsonWithLimit` helper; replaces both `await response.json()` calls
- `extensions/vault/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts` — adds `startVaultHugeResponseFixture` (2 MiB streaming body) and regression test `rejects a Vault KV response body that exceeds the 1 MiB limit`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OOM vulnerability on the Vault KV and JWT-login success-JSON paths; oversized Vault responses now rejected with a bounded error.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `resolveFromVault` → `readVaultSecret` / `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` → `fetchVault` → `readJsonWithLimit` (formerly `response.json()`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real `node:http` `createServer` fixture on `127.0.0.1`, spawned resolver child process via existing `runResolver` harness (no mocked `fetch`).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** `vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` is a standalone static asset with a test-enforced `not.toContain("openclaw/plugin-sdk")` guard. `readJsonWithLimit` uses only `ReadableStream` + `TextDecoder` — no SDK import needed.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22.22.0, source checkout on branch `fix/vault-bound-json-responses`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vault/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

target.title: fix(restart-sentinel): log DB errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## Summary

`clearRestartSentinel`, `readRestartSentinel`, and `hasRestartSentinel` used empty `catch {}` / `catch { return null }` / `catch { return false }` blocks that silently swallowed SQLite DB errors. This PR replaces them with `sentinelLog.warn(...)` so errors are visible in diagnostics while preserving the best-effort semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, three exported functions silently discard all errors from the SQLite state database:

- **`clearRestartSentinel`** — `catch {}`: If the DB write fails (locked, corrupt, disk full), the sentinel is not cleared but the caller has no way to detect this. The gateway may continue to believe a restart is pending.
- **`readRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return null }`: Any DB read error (transient lock, corruption) is treated identically to "no sentinel exists", potentially causing a pending restart to be silently dropped.
- **`hasRestartSentinel`** — `catch { return false }`: Same problem — DB errors are indistinguishable from "no sentinel".

**Code evidence**: In `restart-sentinel.ts:228`, the `catch {}` on the `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` call provides no visibility into whether the sentinel was actually cleared.

## Root Cause

The functions were written with best-effort semantics (they must not throw during shutdown/cleanup), but the empty catch blocks went too far by discarding all diagnostic information. Unlike the intentional best-effort pattern in `ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` (which includes a comment explaining why the catch is empty), these catch blocks had no explanation and no logging.

## Why This Fix

Follows the same pattern accepted in:
- [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) (`fix(delivery): log failDelivery errors instead of silently swallowing`) by @SebTardif
- [#82943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82943) (`fix(agents): log warnings instead of swallowing subagent errors`) by @SebTardif

Uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart-sentinel")` + `formatErrorMessage(err)` — consistent with `restart.ts` which also uses `createSubsystemLogger("restart")`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Operators had no diagnostic signal when the restart sentinel could not be cleared or read — failures were completely invisible.
- **After**: A warning is emitted to the diagnostics log (`[restart-sentinel]` prefix) with the full error context, while the functions continue to return safe defaults (`null` / `false` / `undefined`).

## Evidence

- **Before**: No warnings emitted on stderr when the DB operation fails — errors are silently swallowed.
- **After**: Three warnings emitted with full error context; functions return safely without throwing.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, `catch {}`)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
      The catch blocks are silently swallowing errors.
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-restart-sentinel-catch.mjs
=== clearRestartSentinel ===
clearRestartSentinel completed without throwing

=== readRestartSentinel ===
readRestartSentinel returned: null

=== hasRestartSentinel ===
hasRestartSentinel returned: false

=== stderr (warnings captured) ===
PASS: Warnings were emitted on stderr:
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to clear restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to read restart sentinel: ...
  [restart-sentinel] Failed to check restart sentinel: ...
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed (no lint errors)
- Added 3 regression tests in `restart-sentinel.test.ts` verifying that each function survives DB failures without throwing and returns the safe default value
